item.title: Public sector accounting, audit, and accountability practices in a time of grand challenges
item.content:encoded:
Ricardo Rocha de Azevedo, University of Sao Paulo

Nives Botica Redmayne, Massey University

Alessandro Giosi, Lumsa University

Giorgia Mattei, Roma Tre University

This special issue examines how public sector accounting, auditing, and accountability practices support institutional governance amid global challenges including climate change, digital transformation, and fiscal pressures. The collection recognizes that while international accounting standards promote transparency, significant variations exist in implementation. Expanded reporting frameworks now incorporate sustainability indicators, though digital technologies introduce new governance risks.

The special issue seeks both enabling and critical perspectives on accounting's role in public governance. It explores how accounting information, risk management, and performance measurement strengthen institutional capacity to respond to and anticipate challenges, enhance resilience, and support sustainable decision-making. It also examines whether existing accounting systems may constrain responses or generate unintended consequences.

  • Critical perspectives on accounting practices
  • Accounting, accountability, and societal impact

item.title: Rethinking Local Government Financial Management and Accountability through Comparative Perspectives
item.content:encoded:
Emanuele Padovani, University of Bologna

Christine Martell, University of Colorado Denver

Sungho Park, University of Alabama

Eric Scorsone, University of Virginia

This special issue addresses the underexplored comparative dimension of local government financial management and accountability. While international initiatives have increased access to harmonized data on subnational public finance, they typically adopt a macroeconomic perspective and overlook managerial dimensions at the level of individual local governments. The special issue seeks to advance understanding of how different institutional settings, fiscal arrangements, and governance traditions shape local financial management across national borders.

The call invites papers examining financial data comparability, interactions between fiscal balance and sustainable development, digitalization in public finance, fiscal regulation models, crisis resilience, climate finance accounting, and use of financial information in decision-making. The collection aims to foster dialogue between academics, policymakers, and practitioners to promote integrated approaches to assessing local public finance and enable cities worldwide to strengthen their financial governance.
